draft.title: Linearising data
card: A straight line is the easiest graph to judge. If a relationship is not linear, we can transform one variable so the graph becomes a straight line.
For a pendulum, the period T depends on length L by T = 2π√(L/g). Plotting T² against L gives a straight line through the origin.
A straight line through the origin means the plotted quantities are directly proportional. A curve on the first graph shows the relationship is not linear.
The gradient of the line has a physical meaning. For T² against L, gradient = 4π²/g, so g = 4π² ÷ gradient. The gradient has units too: the units of the y-axis divided by the units of the x-axis.
draft.remember: Plot the transformed quantity so the points form a straight line, then read the physics from the gradient.

a.q: Students plot T² (s²) against L (m) for a pendulum and get a straight line through the origin. What does the gradient allow them to find?
opts: The value of g, using g = 4π² ÷ gradient
The value of L, using L = 4π² ÷ gradient
The mass of the bob, using the gradient
The amplitude of the swing, using the gradient
a.why: For T² against L, the gradient equals 4π²/g, so g can be found by rearranging. Mass and amplitude do not appear in this relationship, so the gradient does not give them.
a.clue: Which quantity is in the gradient formula 4π²/g?

b.q: A student measures the period T of a pendulum at several lengths L and plots T against L. The points form a curve. Which change would be expected to give a straight line?
opts: Plot T² on the vertical axis against L
Plot L on the vertical axis against T
Plot T against L with a larger scale
Draw a line of best fit through the curve
b.why: Since T² = (4π²/g)L, plotting T² against L gives a straight line. Swapping the axes leaves the curve, as L is proportional to T², not T. A bigger scale or a straight line drawn through curved data does not change the relationship.
b.clue: Which transformed quantity is proportional to L?

a.best: The value of g, using g = 4π² ÷ gradient

b.best: Plot T² on the vertical axis against L

problems.detail: The clue 'Which quantity is in the gradient formula 4π²/g?' points straight at g, so a student can pick the answer without understanding linearisation.

check.summary: The physics is correct (T² = 4π²L/g, so g = 4π² ÷ gradient) and both questions have a single right answer. The only problem is that question a's clue names the gradient formula containing g, which gives the answer away.

a.q: Students plot T² (s²) against L (m) for a pendulum and get a straight line through the origin. What does the gradient allow them to find?
opts: The value of g, using g = 4π² ÷ gradient
The value of L, using L = 4π² ÷ gradient
The mass of the bob, using the gradient
The amplitude of the swing, using the gradient
a.why: Squaring both sides gives T² = (4π²/g)L, so the gradient equals 4π²/g and g can be found by rearranging. L is plotted on the x-axis, so it varies along the line and is not a single value from the gradient. Mass and amplitude do not appear in the relationship at all.
a.clue: Square both sides of T = 2π√(L/g) and compare it with y = mx.
